text: dsh-reliability-guards 为 DSH 网页端提供回答校验和操作前保护。插件在会话结束前比对回答与工具结果，发现虚报成功、未实际调用工具却声称已检查、未核实 DOI 等情况时，会提示模型在本轮改写；网页界面会显示检查结果。它也能在用户开启 /explain 后限制会修改内容的工具，并在覆盖已有文件等操作前请求确认。适合使用 DSH 本地模型、希望减少不实回答并控制写操作的用户。检查回答中的 DOI 时会向 OpenAlex 和 Crossref 查询 DOI；不需要 API 密钥。

dsh-reliability-guards checks DSH answers against tool results and prompts revisions for false success claims, unperformed actions, and unchecked DOIs. It can restrict modifying tools in /explain mode and ask before file overwrites. DOI checks query OpenAlex and Crossref; no API key is needed.
DSH 本地模型说操作成功，但工具刚才报错了，能提醒它重新核对回答吗？
我想先让模型只解释方案，等我同意后再执行会改动内容的工具。
模型回答里提到一个 DOI 时，能否检查它是否真实存在？
dsh-reliability-guards 的功能「回答与工具结果校验」：在轮次结束前检查虚报成功、没有工具调用却声称已执行、未核实 DOI 等情况，并将发现合并为提示交给模型改写。
dsh-reliability-guards 的功能「操作前控制与只读解释」：/explain 模式下拒绝未获准的修改工具；执行可能覆盖已有文件的 write 或破坏性命令时，可先向用户请求确认。
dsh-reliability-guards 使用前须知：回答中未从对话工具结果核实的 DOI 会被发送到 OpenAlex 查询，未找到时再查询 Crossref；不需要 API 密钥。

dsh-reliability-guards README · dsh-reliability-guards：Guardrails for small local models in [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (DSH).
Small models (7-35B on Ollama or similar) tend to claim success after a failed command, say they
checked something without calling a tool, invent DOIs, or cut an answer in the middle. This plugin
catches those cases **before the user reads the answer** and lets the model correct itself.

> **Maintenance:** best-effort. Issues may go unanswered; forks are welcome.

dsh-reliability-guards README · What it does：When the turn is about to close, plain deterministic rules compare the final answer with what the
tools really returned. On a finding the model receives **one** steering notice in the same turn
(at most 2 per turn, one per code) and rewrites its answer. What is still wrong at the end stays
visible under the answer.

dsh-reliability-guards README · What it does：| Code | Detected when |
|---|---|
| `falseSuccess` | the answer claims success, but a tool call failed (error, or shell `[exit code: N]`) and was never made up for |
| `actionWithoutTool` | "I checked / I ran ..." with zero tool calls in the turn |
| `announcedOnly` | an action is announced ("let me check:") and nothing is called |
| `deniedCapability` | "I can't access ..." while a fitting tool is in the request |
| `unverifiedDoi` | a DOI in the answer appears in no tool result; the harness checks OpenAlex then Crossref and only an unknown DOI triggers the notice (a network error never counts as invented) |
| `foreignScript` | CJK characters the user did not write |
| `markupLeak` | a tool call written as text (`<tool_call>`, `<function=...>`, `</think>`) |
| `cutAnswer` | the answer ends mid-sentence or with an unclosed code block |
| `emoji` (off by default) | emojis the user did not write |
| `frenchSpelling` (off by default) | misspelled words, checked offline with `enchant-2` |

dsh-reliability-guards README · What it does：Rules are bilingual (English and French phrasing).

**Answer checks** (on the commands the answer gives the user):

dsh-reliability-guards README · What it does：| Code | Detected when |
|---|---|
| `codeWhileWaiting` | you asked to explain first and wait for your validation ("wait for my approval", "attends ma validation"...), and the answer contains code; the wait lasts until you give the go-ahead ("go ahead", "je valide"...) |
| `unknownCommand` | a command in a shell block is not installed on this computer, is not installed by the answer itself, and appears in no tool result (an invented tool presented as real) |
| `untestedCommand` | after a turn with tools: a key, schema, path or option value in a command appears in no tool result of the conversation; lines marked `# untested` (or `# non testé`) pass |
| `shellMistake` | wrong `dconf` syntax (a key ending with `/`, `dump`/`list` on a path without it) |
| `sourcesDenied` | the model read web pages, then says it used no source or lists a "Sources" section without links |

dsh-reliability-guards README · What it does：All findings of one stop go back to the model in **one** message, so it rewrites its answer once.
And what can be known before the answer is written (the wait, your explicit demands such as
"check the installed version", the Sources line, dconf syntax) is told to the model **while it
works**, so most answers are right the first time.

dsh-reliability-guards README · What it does：**Before a tool runs**
- Approval card for destructive shell commands (`rm`, `mv`, `git reset --hard`, `git push --force`,
  `dd`, `>` onto an existing file, `cp` onto an existing file, ...) and for `write` over an existing
  file. Creating new files never asks.
- Backups into `/tmp` are refused with the reason (the folder is emptied between commands).
- `/explain` read-only mode: only an allow-list of tools (reads, searches, proposals) runs;
  everything else is refused, including tools added later. Type `/explain off` to leave it.
  Install the skill: `cp -r skills/explain ~/.dsh/skills/` (or into your `$DSH_HOME/skills`).

dsh-reliability-guards README · What it does：**Skills survive summaries**: when an automatic summary hides the instructions of a skill the user
invoked (`/word`, ...), they are re-sent.

The Web UI shows, under each turn with a finding, what was seen and whether the model corrected it.
English and French UI.

dsh-reliability-guards README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-reliability-guards

dsh-reliability-guards README · or straight from GitHub:：dsh plugin --profile web add github:MathieuPortmann/dsh-reliability-guards
```

Restart the profile afterwards. Requires Node `^22.19.0 || >=24` and DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0` (see [Compatibility](#compatibility)).

dsh-reliability-guards README · Configuration：Row `reliability-guards` in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. Every guard has an on/off switch:
`falseSuccess`, `actionWithoutTool`, `announcedOnly`, `deniedCapability`, `unverifiedDoi`,
`cutAnswer`, `foreignScript`, `emoji`, `frenchSpelling`, `codeWhileWaiting`, `unknownCommand`,
`untestedCommand`, `shellMistake`, `sourcesDenied`, `answerRules` (the rules told before the answer),
`destructiveAsk`, `tmpBackupDeny`, `explainMode`, `keepInvokedSkills`.

dsh-reliability-guards README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxNudgesPerTurn` | 2 | steering notices per turn for the rules (the answer checks have 2 more) |
| `doiTimeoutMs` | 15000 | timeout of each DOI existence check |
| `spellAllow` | `[]` | extra words the spell check accepts |
| `explainAllow` | `[]` | extra tools allowed in `/explain` |
| `llmBodyTimeoutMinutes` | 0 | raise the HTTP body timeout for slow local models (0 = Node default, 5 min) |

dsh-reliability-guards README · Compatibility：| Component | Supported |
|---|---|
| Node.js | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` (`engines.node`) |
| DSH | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`; declared as optional `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (`>=3.18.0 <4.0.0`) and `zod` (`>=4.0.0 <5.0.0`), the packages the plugin loads from the DSH installation (`undici` is also tried, and skipped if absent) |
| Platform | Linux (tested); the plugin itself is pure JavaScript with no native addon |
dsh-reliability-guards README · Compatibility：Tested with DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.2` on Node 22.23 (see [Verification](#verification)).

dsh-reliability-guards README · Permissions and external services：| Capability | Where | Used for | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Files (read only)** | `index.js` (`statSync`) | checks whether the target of `>` / `cp` / `mv` already exists, so only an overwrite asks for approval | treated as "does not exist": no approval card |
| **Files (read only)** | `index.js` (`accessSync`, `statSync`) | answer checks: whether a program named in an answer is installed (executable in a `PATH` folder, or in `/usr/sbin`, `/sbin`, `/snap/bin`, `/var/lib/flatpak/exports/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`), and whether a file path named in a command of the answer exists. Only existence is checked; no file is opened or read | treated as "not installed" / "does not exist": the model is asked to check it |
| **Memory** | `index.js` | answer checks: the tool arguments and full tool results of each conversation (last ~400k characters), so a name in an answer can be compared with what the tools really showed. In memory only, never written to disk, gone when DSH stops | n/a |
| **Files (write)** | none | the plugin writes nothing; its state lives in the DSH session log | n/a |
| **Network** | `lib/

dsh-reliability-guards README · Permissions and external services：The plugin also *blocks* actions: it asks for approval before destructive shell commands, refuses
backups into `/tmp`, and in `/explain` mode refuses every tool outside an allow-list. It adds no
tool of its own and runs no command on behalf of the model.

dsh-reliability-guards README · Verification：Checked on a disposable profile (`DSH_HOME` pointing at a temporary folder, profile cloned with
`dsh <name> --from-default-profile web`, so the real profile is never touched):

```sh
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile t add file:$PWD/dsh-reliability-guards-0.1.1.tgz   # install
dsh --profile t --no-open --port 3095                                    # start: plugin loads, no error
dsh plugin --profile t remove dsh-reliability-guards                      # uninstall

dsh-reliability-guards README · Verification：`npm test` runs 49 standalone tests (rules, patterns, answer checks, DOI extraction, spell check
parsing, kept skills, load test of the real module) with no DSH installation needed except the load test, which
skips when DSH is absent.

dsh-reliability-guards README · Develop：```sh
npm test
```
